findings.title: "Silence notifications" does nothing in the list view: the drawer needs a ruler rule
findings.body: In the list view `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} .../>` with no `rule` (ruler) prop. `AlertRuleMenu` shows "Silence notifications" for it, because `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` returns `canSilence` (the new test asserts that the item is present). Clicking it calls `handleSilence`, which sets `showSilenceDrawer`. The drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. `rule` is `undefined` here, so nothing renders and the click has no effect and no error. `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` (`components/silences/SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer.tsx`) only reads `rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid`. Only the UID is needed, so the drawer should accept a UID (or the prom rule's `uid`) and render for the prom-only case. Until then, don't offer the menu item. The new tests never click Silence, which is how this was missed.

findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items are unreachable in the list view, though their abilities are computed
findings.body: `canPause` and `canDelete` are now computed from the Grafana prom-rule abilities (lines 83 and 87). The render conditions still need a ruler rule: pause needs `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` (line 123) and delete needs `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). The list view passes only `promRule`, so Pause and Delete disappear from the menu for every Grafana rule there. Before this change the list loaded the ruler group and offered both. The permission code for the prom path is dead for these two actions. `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:206-207` asserts exactly 4 menu items and defines `ui.menuItems.delete` without using it. That locks the regression in, even though the test grants `AlertingRuleDelete` and `AlertingRuleUpdate`. Either render these items from `promRule`/`identifier` (`MenuItemPauseRule` and `handleDelete` take a ruler rule today, so they need prom-based variants), or state in the PR that dropping them is intended. If the removal is intended, remove the dead ability plumbing.

findings.title: Federated-group check dropped from the legacy `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` path
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which makes the rule immutable (no edit, delete, pause). It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` (line 245, behind a TODO). `isFederatedRuleGroup` (`utils/rules.ts:373`) checks `group.source_tenants`, and `useCombinedRuleNamespaces.ts:256` still populates it. The legacy hook is still used by `components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx:57` (edit ability) and `RuleDetailsButtons.tsx`. So Mimir federated rule groups can now show Edit and Delete in the legacy list, where they were blocked before. Keep the federated check in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`, for example by passing it into the shared implementation or by AND-ing the result, until the TODO is done.

findings.title: Prom-rule abilities treat "alerting rule" as "Grafana rule", so recording rules lose Export, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently
findings.body: The ruler-based hook uses `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which covers alerting and recording rules. The new hook uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` for `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently` (lines 324-328). The comment above it says "All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition", which is the condition the ruler hook used. For Grafana recording rules the new path therefore returns not-supported for these actions where the ruler path allowed them. The visible effect today is that Export is hidden for recording rules in the list view. Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these abilities and keep `alertingRule` only for Silence, which is alerting-only (the ruler path excludes recording rules there too).

findings.title: Rule link no longer carries `returnTo`
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` built the link with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new item uses `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`. `DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36` still adds it. Without it, opening a Grafana rule from the list and navigating back from the rule page loses the list state, such as filters and the expanded folder. Restore `createReturnTo()` here. The new test only checks `stringContaining('/alerting/grafana/<uid>/view')`, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Stale comments: the loader no longer uses the Ruler endpoint
findings.body: The component doc says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints" (line 25) and the `expectedRulesCount` doc mentions the Ruler response (line 19). The Ruler query is gone. The "Creating" and "Deleting" operation items are gone with it, and `GrafanaRuleListItem` still accepts an `operation` prop that no caller passes. Update the docs and drop the unused prop, or say why it is kept.

findings.title: Stale name and comment after removing the ruler prefetch
findings.body: The comment above says "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules", and the variable is still called `cacheAndRulerPreload`. After the change it only upserts the Prometheus group cache. Rename it (for example `cachePromGroups`) and fix the comment.

findings.title: Leftover "// duplicate" comment
findings.body: `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` is an unexplained stray comment, and the preceding comment already says what the hook is. Remove it, or say what is duplicated. The hook largely repeats the Grafana branch of `useIsRuleEditable`, so that duplication may be what it means.

findings.title: Menu test doesn't exercise the actions and has a hardcoded count
findings.body: The test only checks that items exist and that there are exactly 4. It never clicks Silence (which currently does nothing, see `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104`). It never asserts that Delete or Pause are absent or present, and `ui.menuItems.delete` is defined but unused. A `toBe(4)` count also passes while the Delete and Pause items are missing. Add a Silence-click test that expects the drawer, and assert on Delete and Pause explicitly. Once Pause and Delete are restored, update the expected items.

contracts.action: List view rule row renders actions from the Prometheus rule only (no ruler fetch)
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx GrafanaRuleListItem, which passed both `rule={rulerRule}` and `promRule` to RuleActionsButtons.V2
contracts.before_after: Before: ruler group fetched, so every ruler-gated menu item and the silence drawer worked. After: `rule` is undefined and only `promRule` is passed, so abilities come from `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` and the identifier is built from `promRule.uid`.
contracts.visible_effect: Edit, Silence, Duplicate, Export and Copy link appear. Pause and Delete no longer appear. Clicking Silence opens nothing.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent no-op on Silence click. If the folder fetch is pending, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns not-editable, so Edit is hidden until the folder loads.

contracts.before_after: Before: federated groups were immutable. After: `isFederated` is hardcoded false.
contracts.visible_effect: Edit and Delete can appear for federated Mimir rules in the legacy list (RuleActionsButtons.tsx).
contracts.failure_mode: Silent permission widening in the UI. The backend should still reject, but the UI no longer hides the actions.

contracts.action: Provenance read from the Prometheus rule DTO to mark rules immutable
contracts.before_after: The Prometheus Grafana rules endpoint sets `Provenance` per rule in `toRuleGroup`, so the new field should be populated.
contracts.visible_effect: Provisioned rules are not editable in the list view.
contracts.failure_mode: If the JSON tag differs from `provenance`, every rule would look unprovisioned and Edit would show for provisioned rules. I did not read the JSON tag.
contracts.open_question: Is the `provenance` JSON key on the Go `apimodels.AlertingRule`/`RecordingRule` types exactly `provenance`?

summary:
The list view now builds its actions from the Prometheus rule alone, and two of those actions are broken. "Silence notifications" shows in the menu, but clicking it opens nothing, because the drawer still needs a ruler rule. Pause and Delete never render for list items, even though their abilities are computed. The new `GrafanaGroupLoader` test asserts exactly 4 menu items, so it locks that in.

Other behaviour changes:
- **Federated groups:** the legacy `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` lost its federated-group check, so Edit and Delete can reappear for federated Mimir groups.
- **Recording rules:** the new Grafana ability hook uses "alerting rule" where the old one used "Grafana rule", so recording rules lose Export and Pause.
- **Rule links:** list-item links no longer carry `returnTo`.

I also left three smaller comments: stale docs in `GrafanaGroupLoader`, a stale name and comment in `prometheusGroupsGenerator`, and a stray `// duplicate` comment in `useAbilities.ts`.

I did not confirm that the backend's JSON key for `provenance` is exactly `provenance`; that is the one open contract. I only read these files and did not run any tests.
